title: Finite-presentation realization near the infinitesimal locus
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Separated, finite type and proper morphisms use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally finitely presented on etale scheme charts. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it has a presentation $\mathcal O^r\to\mathcal O^s\to F\to0$ with $r,s$ finite. Base-flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the corresponding local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. Proper support means there exist a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $G$ on $Z$ such that $i_*G\simeq F$ [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $(A_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse sequence of commutative rings with surjective transition maps whose kernels are locally nilpotent, meaning every element of each kernel is nilpotent, and set $A=\varprojlim_n A_n$. Let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and finitely presented, put $X_n=X\times_A\operatorname{Spec}A_n$, and put $X_0=|X_1|\subseteq|X|$, the common underlying closed subset of all the $X_n$. For every $n\geq1$ let $M_n$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-module, flat over $A_n$, with support proper over $A_n$, with specified isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_{A_n}A_{n-1}\simeq M_{n-1}$ for $n\geq2$. There exist an open subspace $W\subseteq X$ containing $X_0$, a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_W$-module $F$, and isomorphisms $F\otimes_A A_n\simeq M_n$ for all $n$, compatible with the specified transition isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 0CX4 (situation-existence), 0CX5 (lemma-compute-what-it-should-be) through 0CX9 (lemma-finitely-presented); existence consequence of 0CX9, with its canonical projection maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-derived-limit] to the specified tower. Obtain the bounded quasi-coherent object $K$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for $i<0$ and projection maps $q_n:K\to M_n$ satisfying $q_{n-1}=t_nq_n$. Set $F_*=H^0(K)$ and let $a_n=H^0(q_n):F_*\to M_n$. We will restrict this single quasi-coherent module; hence no gluing of independently chosen modules or isomorphisms will be needed.

Fix $x\in X_0$. Choose an affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to X$ and $u\in U$ above $x$ with $B$ finitely presented over $A$; such charts exist by the stated chartwise finite-presentation hypothesis. Choose generators of $B$ and a polynomial surjection $P=A[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\twoheadrightarrow B$. By [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-polynomial-model], take a bounded-above finite-free $P$-complex $E^\bullet$ representing $R\Gamma(U,K)$, also after principal localization. By [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-affine-base-change] and its K-flat calculation, $E^\bullet\otimes_A A_n$ has cohomology only in degree zero, where the projection-induced identification is $\Gamma(U_n,M_n)$. Here affine etale realization [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] applies to $U_n$ and to $U$: it identifies module cohomology with sheaf cohomology and detects zero objects. In particular $R\Gamma(U,K)$ has no negative cohomology. All these assertions hold again on a principal open of $U$, using the same cited localized model and base-change theorem.

source.place: Tags 0CX7, 0CX8 and 0CX9, choice of affine chart and polynomial model.

proof.text: We now remove positive terms by finite downward induction on an upper bound $t$ for $E^\bullet$. If $t\leq0$ there is nothing to remove. If $t>0$ and $E^t\ne0$, then $\operatorname{coker}(E^{t-1}\to E^t)\otimes_A A_1=0$, since it is the top cohomology of the reduced complex. The prime of $P$ corresponding to $u$ contains $\ker(A\to A_1)P$, so the matrix of this differential is surjective over its residue field. Some maximal minor is therefore nonzero there. Invert its determinant, retaining $u$. Reorder its columns and multiply the corresponding square block by its inverse: the differential becomes $[I\ D]$. The change of coordinates $(v,w)\mapsto(v-Dw,w)$ makes it $[I\ 0]$, with a free complementary kernel. Since consecutive differentials compose to zero, the preceding differential lands in that kernel. Thus an identity two-term complex splits off in degrees $t-1,t$, and deleting it is a chain homotopy equivalence, also after tensoring with every $A_n$. Replace $t$ by $t-1$ and repeat. Finitely many such steps yield a principal neighborhood $U^\prime\subset U$ of $u$ and a bounded-above finite-free complex $G^\bullet$ over a principal localization $P^\prime$ of $P$, with $G^i=0$ for $i>0$, representing the restriction of $K$ and all its derived reductions. Zero top ranks are simply omitted.

source.place: Tag 0CX9, maximal-rank argument and induction; explicit invertible-block cancellation.

proof.text: Put $B^\prime=\Gamma(U^\prime,\mathcal O)$ and $C=H^0(G^\bullet)=\operatorname{coker}(G^{-1}\to G^0)$. This is finitely presented over $P^\prime$. Its action factors through $P^\prime\twoheadrightarrow B^\prime$, because it is $H^0(R\Gamma(U^\prime,K))$. Tensoring this finite presentation with $B^\prime$ gives a finite presentation of $C$ over $B^\prime$, since $C\otimes_{P^\prime}B^\prime=C$. Affine realization [lem-sfb-affine-etale-derived-module-realization] identifies the associated sheaf of $C$ with $F_*|_{U^\prime}$. Since $G^{>0}=0$, right exactness of tensor identifies $H^0(G^\bullet\otimes_A A_n)=C\otimes_A A_n$. The projection-induced base-change isomorphism [lem-sfb-space-inverse-module-affine-base-change] therefore identifies $a_n$ on this chart with an isomorphism $C\otimes_A A_n\simeq\Gamma(U_n^\prime,M_n)$. This proves finite presentation and every required reduction on the chart.

source.place: Tag 0CX9, the case with highest degree at most zero and its canonical projection maps.

proof.text: By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image], the image $W_x$ of $U^\prime\to X$ is an open subspace containing $x$, and $U^\prime\to W_x$ is surjective etale. Let $W=\bigcup_{x\in X_0}W_x$ and set $F=F_*|_W$. On the etale covering family $U^\prime\to W$, step 4 gives a finite presentation, so $F$ is finitely presented by the etale-local definition in the statement. Every $X_n\to X$ factors through $W$ because its underlying image is $X_0\subset W$. The maps $a_n$ induce $F\otimes_A A_n\to M_n$ there. Their restrictions to the covering charts are the isomorphisms of step 4, so they are isomorphisms (local inverses agree on overlaps by uniqueness). Finally $a_{n-1}=H^0(t_n)a_n$; on a tensor $m\otimes b$, both transition composites send it to $b\,a_{n-1}(m)$. The isomorphisms therefore respect the specified transitions, not just the underlying isomorphism classes. If $X_0$ is empty, take $W=\varnothing$ and $F=0$; all $X_n$ are empty.
